title: F35c: bind a route:lane override on MEMBERSHIP — inject both manifest projections as one port
summary: F35 (fix/routing-parity-seed-plan) makes a declared protected FILE bind (route:lane cannot relax it) by combining the injected SCOPE predicate with inboxbatch's file-spelling rule, because for a file spelling scope IS membership. A declared DIRECTORY that is itself inside a protected directory fragment (go/internal/bridge/, .evolve/build-explanation-contracts/) or an extensionless member prefix (go/internal/phases/audit/probe_quarantine) still reads as scope and stays overridable, although every card file under it is refused by triage's breaker (membership). Architecture review 2026-09-26, MAJOR M1 (deferred, not a regression; no live item has this shape).
fix: Inject both projections as ONE port built at the composition roots, e.g. inboxbatch.Surface{Member: guards.IsProtectedSurface, Scope: guards.IsProtectedScope}: routed = Scope(tok), binding = Member(tok), mentions judged with Member; inboxbatch then holds no spelling rule (drop the isFileSpelling coupling for binding). Mechanical across the six routing roots (cmd_inbox.go, phases/triage/triage.go prompt partition, triagecap wave_seed/ReadInboxBacklog, inboxmover claim floor, loopwave Ports.Protected/routedBase, core triage_termination nil) and their ports/tests.
acceptance: RED first: a test walks guards.ProtectedSurfaceManifest and, for each fragment, builds an operator route:lane item declaring that fragment as a token and asserts ConsoleRouted routes it (fails today on the directory fragments and the probe_quarantine prefix).
An operator route:lane over a declared directory that merely CONTAINS protected files (go/internal/core/) is still honored.
No behavior change for file spellings (TestConsoleRouted_LaneOverrideCannotRelaxAProtectedFile stays green).
notes: Console-owned by kind. Evidence + design: docs/research/verification-wave-findings-2026-09-14.md F35 (Residual) and the ADR-0074 F34/F35 amendment.
